killed.claim: Named culinary substitutes co-move MORE than category-matched non-substitute pairs — the shared-episode rate for the {n}

fatal.problem: The core statistic is the undirected pair score the site retired of record. `cavg(a,b)=(cdir(a,b)+cdir(b,a))/2` symmetrizes a measure that `cost-index/co-movement.json`'s `_doc`, `scripts/lib/cost-events-analysis.mjs:12-14` ("never a global undirected pair count, which would over-imply a relationship"), and ADR-015 Decision 1 all require to stay directed and anchored. ADR-015's own worked example of the asymmetry that must be preserved — "chicken-breast→thigh 5/6 is not thigh→breast 5/5" — is exactly the pair the finding leads with, collapsed into a 0.917 that exists in neither direction. Every headline number, the top-10 entanglement table, and the 16-zero-pairs list rest on that measure. Not fixable by caveat; requires re-derivation in the directed measure.

The claim is prior art twice over and its residual novelty is definitional. Externally, Pindyck & Rotemberg (1990) already own "a co-moving swap does not hedge" — and it is already reference [29] in /cost-index/menu-pricing/study/index.html, whose own evidence table (offset ~159227) records exactly that myth as corrected. Internally, the site already publishes the strictly-more-useful per-pair form: 94 hedge/mirror verdicts with k/n in data/ingredient-depth.json, `comover`/`comover_shared`/`comover_of` in cost-index/menu-pricing.json (chicken-breast → "Chicken thigh", 5 of 6), "moved with chicken thigh" on five live event cards, a full study section "The swap that helps versus the swap that mirrors," an FAQ, an llms.txt owned question, and completed task #36. The only incremental element — the category-matched control — is carried by pairs that are the same species or the same animal (6 Lactuca sativa lettuce pairs, cherry tomato/tomato, broccoli/cauliflower, chicken breast/thigh = 8 of its own top 10), tested against different-crop controls, so it restates a botanical and butchery identity rather than a market relationship.

killed.claim: The 11 ingredients withheld for reason='flat' are not flat markets — they are dead price-discovery: their public wholesa

fatal.problem: The permutation test's exchangeability assumption is violated and the headline median is a single-desk artifact: 5 of the 10 Group A series are one AMS Boston herb table (identical start 2024-01-10, identical n=130, same source, synchronized change weeks — tarragon/thyme both change 2025-01-22 and 2025-01-29; oregano/thyme both 2026-01-21 and 2026-01-28), a 6th (rutabaga) is the same desk, and the reported median (2 of 51 changes) is set by that block. Effective n for Group A is about 6 reporting blocks, not 10, so "0 of 10,000 relabelings, p = 0.00000" is not a valid p-value. Compounding it, the label itself is a near-deterministic function of the outcome (reason='flat' <- degenerate <- halfWidthPct < 0.003 <- the same one-step residual vector whose nonzero fraction IS the change rate, cost-lockfloat.js:63 / cost-conformal.js:155-157), so the null is falsified by construction and the discovery window only defers it via one-year persistence the finding itself documents. And the claim is factually false for 3 of the 10 — kale 17/51 (17 distinct values in 52 rows), collard-greens 19/51 in discovery, carrot 11/51 are not dead quotes; the non-independent median hides a bimodal group.

The claim's central assertion — "are not flat markets — they are dead price-discovery," with "administratively sticky quotes" pinned on named USDA AMS desks — is an unsourced causal attribution that the finding's own caveat 7 says the statistic cannot make ("it shows the reported number did not move, and those are exactly the two things this statistic cannot separate"). It fits none of the three permitted patterns in docs/fact-check.md, and it publishes something stronger than the site's own shipped copy for the same label (tools/_shared/cost-lockfloat-ui.js:44: "flat and stale — nothing to call"). Compounding it, the contamination half is largely a restatement of the classifier's definition (cost-lockfloat.js:73-75 with cost-conformal.js:150-157 force low-change-rate series into the lock bucket), so the second sentence is an artifact presented as a discovery.

The headline restates copy the site already publishes for this exact set — "flat and stale — nothing to call" (tools/_shared/cost-lockfloat-ui.js:44, live on /tools/cost-pulse/) — and restates the labeling rule itself: all 11 flat items carry halfWidthPct/upPct/downPct exactly 0 in data/cost-lockfloat.json, meaning the label is assigned because the quote did not move. Staleness in thin AMS terminal quotes is additionally standard, source-annotated practice (the AMS FV020 reports flag "offerings light" on basil, oregano, rosemary, thyme, cilantro). And it is not actionable: these 11 are already withheld, and the implied action is verbatim the site's existing withhold CTA at cost-lockfloat-ui.js:520-521.

killed.claim: The lock/cushion/float band fails disproportionately during the exact episodes it is being trusted to survive: across th

fatal.problem: The exposure variable is misconstructed, and the error is differential. data/cost-index-events.json `date` is the episode PEAK and `durationDays` is the shoulder-to-shoulder span STRADDLING it (scripts/build-cost-index-events.mjs:99-107, verified by re-deriving all 337 durations with 0 mismatches), but the analysis scores [date, date + durationDays] — an interval whose mean 45.9% lies past the true episode end. 43.0% of "inside" tests (1,664/3,873) are not in an episode and miss at 22.78%, below the outside baseline; 1,615 genuinely in-episode run-up tests, the highest-miss stratum in the data at 50.71%, are scored as controls. Correctly aligned, R = 2.01 (coverage 51.5% inside, 53.4% for lock) — so the headline is conservative, but the published qualification reverses: true mid-episode R = 1.663 (coverage 59.9%), not the 1.068 "recovery" the revised claim builds its operator rule on. That rule tells a lock operator the band is trustworthy again inside a sustained plateau when it is not.

The event windows are mis-registered against the episodes they name. build-cost-index-events.mjs sets `date` to the PEAK and `durationDays` to the full two-sided shoulder span (l..r around that peak), but the finding joins on [date, date + durationDays] — anchored at the peak, running forward by the whole span. The peak sits a median 47.1% into its episode (94.7% of events not at the start), so 1,664 of the 3,873 "inside" tests (43.0%) fall entirely outside the true episode, while the entire run-up — the highest-miss stratum, R = 2.0714 (1,025/2,001) — is scored as "outside." The headline sentence "1,416 of 3,873 prints inside detected event windows" is therefore false, and the edges/interior decomposition that the revised claim's operator rule depends on measures a window that never contained the onset and is ~43% phantom post-episode tail (that tail alone: R = 1.1452, at the finding's own 1.10 calendar floor). Correct registration gives R = 2.0124 — a different number and a different rule.

The publishable payload — "the band is least reliable while a price is entering or leaving a departure" — is conditioned on a hindsight-only label. Event windows come from a CENTERED ±26-week median (build-cost-index-events.mjs:45,114) with forward-expanded durations (:99–104), so "inside/edge of an episode" is not knowable for ~6 months, while the band's coverage is leakage-free walk-forward by construction (cost-conformal.js:77, :16/126/149). An operator can only act on the rule by guessing that a departure is starting — a direction/timing call the surface's own certified copy gate forbids (check-lockfloat-copy.mjs cases direction-will-move / direction-more-likely / opportunity-lock-a-low) and the no-forecast rule bars. Compounding it, the honesty stamp "every level is public wholesale reference, never delivered price" is false for 2 of the 63 series: pork-belly (BLS WPS022104) and vegetable-oil (FRED PCU3112243112243 / BLS WPU0278) are PPI INDEX series with basis "index" and level:null — 536 of 65,932 tests — and our own data/cost-index-sources.json says of vegetable-oil "No free oil price LEVEL exists … honestly directional." Both sit in the lock bucket the claim headlines.

The headline relationship is already published by this site: ADR-022 `coverage-regime-qualifier` (Accepted 2026-07-28) ships the inside-vs-outside-episode coverage split on 134 EN/ES ingredient pages via `scripts/inject-coverage-regime-note.mjs`, gated at `scripts/check-all.mjs:620,641`, stating "77.7% outside a detected price episode and 60.7% during one — a miss rate about 1.8x higher." This finding is the window-26 restatement of that window-52 claim — and ADR-022 Decision 2 explicitly names and rejects the lockfloat `replay` strip as the substrate for this very measurement ("It is a different band"). Compounding it: the direction is standard conformal-under-distribution-shift prior art (ACI / EnbPI / volatility clustering), conceded in the finding's own caveat 1, and the conditioning label is uncomputable in real time (centered ±26-week baseline at `build-cost-index-events.mjs:114`, two-sided duration expansion at `:99-106`, retrospective top-6 ranking at `:119-124`), so the refined operator rule cannot be executed at the moment of decision.

fatal.problem: A debunking null published on a test that cannot support a debunk. The advertised sensitivity is wrong (power at the stated 62% MDE is 0.562, not 0.80; the 80%-power MDE is ~0.68 at n=50 and ~0.70 at the design-effect-corrected n_eff=41.6, ICC 0.0713 by category, plus 4 pairs sharing byte-identical import_seasonal_index so only 46 distinct calendars exist). The pooled null is a cancelling mixture the analysis flagged but never tested: 31 rows with >=10y customs history go 35.5% hits and mean circular distance 3.61, while 14 rows with <=4y go 64.3% and 1.93 (Mann-Whitney p=0.0058 uncorrected), so the headline 2.96~3.0 is an average of two opposite numbers. And the statistic is biased toward the null by construction — customs VALUE = price x quantity under inelastic ag demand makes a heavy-arrival month register as a low-value month — which the finding's own caveat concedes ("cannot adjudicate the folk model as stated") in direct contradiction of its headline sentence.

The pooled null is an aggregation/resolution artifact, not a property of the two calendars. Splitting the 50 rows by the granularity of the import series they are built from — 6-digit HS buckets vs 10-digit HTS statistical lines, a field (`import_hs6`) present in the same data file — yields mean circular distances of 3.72 (n=25, p_align = 0.9924, anti-aligned) and 2.20 (n=25, p_align = 0.0121, aligned). The headline 2.96 is the average of the two; the split itself is significant (permutation p = 0.0013 on the collinear span split, p = 0.0091 after deduping to 46 distinct HS codes). The claim "the tracked import-value record gives no support for reading a price trough off import timing" is false for the half of the sample with item-specific customs lines. The finding named this exact hazard in its caveats and dismissed it as "not separable with these fields," which is factually incorrect.

The claim adjudicates a VOLUME proposition ("heavy-arrival window") using a customs-VALUE series that structurally cannot see volume — the exact value-never-volume breach for which this repo's own adversarial audit already deleted this identical pairing (`buyclock` = cheapest_month × import peak; build-ingredient-state-record.mjs:370-373, 2026-07-18-corpus-expansion-overnight.md:163-165). Compounding it, the finding's own caveat concedes the null is "partly mechanical" because value = price × quantity drags import value down in the same month a price falls, and states outright that it "cannot adjudicate the folk model as stated about physical arrivals" — yet the revisedClaim omits that caveat and concludes the record "gives no support" anyway. A null that is partly an artifact of the metric's construction cannot be published as evidence against the proposition it was built against.

The finding is a restatement of content the site already publishes: scripts/lib/seasonality-fusion.mjs mechanismFor() lines 76-79 performs the identical import_seasonal_index[cheapest_month-1] test, and open/seasonality/index.html lines 595-596 already publishes the resulting split (28 counter-phase / 42 not-import-aligned / 14 no-import-calendar of 84) along with the exact value-never-volume caveat and the "one is not causing the other" line. The same 1.05 threshold on the finding's own 50 rows gives 20/50 = 40%, matching the published 28/70 = 40%. On top of that, docs/handoff/2026-07-18-corpus-expansion-overnight.md lines 163-165 records that the repo's own 4-lens audit already dropped this exact read (`buyclock`) because it breached value-never-volume and "added nothing to a buy the cheapest_month field already decides." No operator decision changes, and the entry itself concedes the import-VALUE series cannot adjudicate a claim about physical arrivals.

killed.claim: An FDA recall on an ingredient does not co-occur with a detected departure in that ingredient's wholesale reference seri

fatal.problem: The power certification that distinguishes this from an uninformative null fails on the finding's own pre-registered threshold. Effective n is 162, not 263, when the design effect is measured on the block-shuffle null that actually sets the critical value (null SD 0.01540 vs naive 0.01031, DEFF 2.23) rather than on a bootstrap of the observed statistic with 9 hits in 6 clusters. 162 < the 191 the finding says is required, so its own VOID branch triggers. Direct simulation against the design's real empirical critical value (0.0691, not the assumed 0.0600) gives power against an exact doubling of 0.625 with event-clustered planting and 0.704 even under a maximally generous iid alternative — never the claimed 0.80. Eighty-percent power begins at roughly 2.2x the null, not 1.84x. The study therefore cannot rule out a doubling of the large-move rate, which is precisely the effect an operator would act on, so the headline "no advance warning" outruns the evidence.

Exposure and outcome are measured in different geographies and at different supply-chain positions, and the corpus cannot fix it. 83% of observations are priced off a single terminal market (LA 53.9%, Boston 29.3%), while 91.5% of recall notices are regional, not nationwide — 242 of 362 observations (66.9%) pair a recall whose distribution states exclude the state of the market setting the price. data/food-recalls.json carries no origin/production field, and many exposures are downstream fresh-cut processors whose recalls remove nothing from wholesale supply (the dataset's own _doc: "a whole-word text match on the product, not an inferred link"). The dilution is asymmetric — mismatched pairs still generate chance hits under the shuffled null but cannot generate causal hits under the alternative — so a doubling among valid exposures moves the pooled rate only 0.0397→0.0528, requiring n≈1,500 against the effective n=263 they claim as adequate. Their own VOID branch fires, and "a measured absence rather than an untested one" is unsupported.

The exposure variable is a whole-word product-text tag that open/recalls/index.html itself publishes as "not a supply or price link" (composite and store-brand goods that merely name the ingredient) — 8 of the 9 headline co-occurrences are rum, supplements, tamales, cream cheese, leeks and sliced cucumber, not the tagged commodity — so "an FDA recall on an ingredient" misdescribes the instrument; and the analysis performs exactly the recall-to-price join that ADR-015's 2026-07-24c addendum forbids and that scripts/check-open-lane-honesty.mjs:59-64 enforces as a required published literal ("never joined to a price") in the page lede, meta/OG description, schema.org Dataset description, dataset note, and the recall section on every cost-index/<slug>/ page.

The conclusion is not new on either axis. Internally, /home/user/potentially-profitable/open/recalls/index.html line 331 already publishes "a recall is never a price signal" and scripts/build-open-recalls-page.mjs enforces a no-price guard around it, so the finding restates the site's own live editorial doctrine. Externally, USDA ERS (spinach 2006: -$202.5M spinach, +$141.9M lettuce) and the meat-recall demand literature established the economics long ago — and they predict a DOWN move in the implicated commodity plus an UP move in substitutes. The code tests up-episodes only (`if x["direction"] == "up"`), reports any-direction 11/362 with no null, and never tests the down direction, so the finding scores a null on the one direction prior art already said would be null. It then pools ~200 single-notice lot recalls (median 1 notice/event across 315 events) with the two genuine national outbreaks, and stratifies only by FDA hazard class (Class I = 426/718 notices), which is not a scale or publicity proxy — so the null is also a dilution of exactly the event class known to move produce markets.

allVerdicts.caveat:
Publish the interval, not the point estimate. The durable effect is roughly +10 percentage points, about 2x — not +17.17pp / 2.8x. Clustering the 30 strata into their 14 genuinely independent ingredient components (one component contains all six lettuce pairs plus both cabbage pairs) and bootstrapping gives a 95% CI of [+10.1pp, +21.0pp] on the difference and [2.07x, 4.12x] on the ratio. Any published sentence must carry that lower bound or say "roughly twice"; "2.8 times" as a bare figure is an over-claim on a point estimate that moves to ~+10pp under every de-clustering, outlier-removal, and drop-rule-restoring variant (one-per-anchor +10.30pp; drop lettuce +10.93pp; drop top-5 +9.76pp; cross-commodity-only +9.85pp).

Three further requirements. (1) State the effective sample size honestly as 14 independent ingredient clusters, not 30 pairs or 23 anchors — the permutation p of 0.0001 assumes 30 independent strata and is optimistic; at one-stratum-per-cluster the median p is 0.0010 with a 95th percentile of 0.0130. (2) Fix the denominator inconsistency: the "32 same-category / 6 cross-category" split comes from the relaxed 38-pair design while the headline 26.9%/9.8% comes from the 30-pair primary — say so explicitly or the two paragraphs do not reconcile. (3) Drop the two-decimal precision on individual pairs. Detection caps at six episodes per ingredient and 65 of 80 anchors sit at exactly n=6, so the measure moves in steps of 0.167; "chicken breast to chicken thigh sits at 0.92" should read "shared five of six" or similar, and it should be named as the single most influential observation in the result (removing it alone moves the headline from +17.17pp to +14.72pp). Retain the existing shared-reporting caveat verbatim — my analysis shows the effect survives removing same-commodity varieties (+9.85pp on 17 cross-commodity pairs, p=0.00055), which strengthens that caveat's honesty but does not retire it.
allVerdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the stratum construction exactly from the three named files (30 strata, mean treatment 0.26944, mean per-stratum control 0.09772, obs +0.17173) and then ran six attacks. Five of the six failed to dent it; the sixth kills the magnitude, not the effect.

ATTACK 1 — STRUCTURAL OPPORTUNITY / SHIFTING DENOMINATOR. This was my best shot and it failed cleanly. `data/cost-index-events.json` has wildly heterogeneous history spans: 63 slugs start 2001 (~25y) but 27 start 2024/2025 (span.years as low as 1.2). Two ingredients whose price histories barely overlap CANNOT share an episode, so if substitute partners systematically had longer-overlapping spans than controls, the whole effect would be a coverage artifact. There IS an asymmetry — mean structural ceiling (fraction of the anchor's events whose ±6wk window intersects the partner's span) is 0.9667 for treatment vs 0.8938 for controls. But conditioning it away does nothing: restricting BOTH arms to full-overlap pairs only (23 strata) gives +17.58pp, p<5e-5 — slightly LARGER. Opportunity-normalising (v/ceiling) gives +16.94pp, p<5e-5. Not a span artifact.

ATTACK 2 — DENOMINATOR ASYMMETRY IN k/n. cavg is (k_ab/n_a + k_ba/n_b)/2, so a small-n partner can only score 0 or 1 and would inflate. Mean n_b = 5.567 vs mean n_c = 5.737; treatment has 2 of 30 partners with n<=2, controls 9 of 251. The asymmetry runs slightly the wrong way for the finding and is far too small to matter.
